name: Delaware Museum of Nature & Science
blurb: The state's natural history museum, on Kennett Pike north of Wilmington. Four galleries, a dinosaur hall, live animal presentations and a Star Lab. It's built for children and doesn't pretend otherwise — under-16s have to have an adult with them the whole way round.

hours.note: Online tickets stop selling at 9am each day. Walk-ins are fine. The Nature Nook keeps shorter hours Tuesday to Thursday, 10am to 3:30pm.

admission.note: $15.50 for anyone 3 and over, $5.50 for toddlers 1 to 2, free under 12 months. Members free. There's a 5% discount for paying cash.

inside: Regional Journey and Global Journey galleries
PaleoZone — the dinosaur hall
The Discovery Gallery
Live animal presentations, Star Lab shows and storytelling
The Rest, Relax & Recharge cafe
warnings: Everyone under 16 must be with an adult for the whole visit.
Online ticket sales close at 9am. After that it's walk-in only.

sources.label: Delaware Museum of Nature & Science: visit
sources.note: The operator. Gives the 9:30am to 4pm hours, the full admission table including the cash discount, the Kennett Pike address, the phone number, the four galleries, the cafe and the under-16 rule. Note the old delmnh.org domain now redirects here.

outstanding: Confirm whether it's open seven days or closes one day a week.
Confirm parking and whether it costs anything.
Ask about step-free access and accessible restrooms.
Confirm holiday closures.

photos.alt: A long low museum building with yellow panels and a sharply angled glass entrance canopy, lawn and driveway in front.
photos.caption: The entrance. The sign in this photograph still reads Delaware Museum of Natural History — the museum was renamed Delaware Museum of Nature & Science after it was taken.

name: Delaware Art Museum
blurb: Pre-Raphaelites, Howard Pyle and the Brandywine illustrators, and a sculpture garden, on Kentmere Parkway. Free parking behind the building, which in Wilmington is worth saying. Thursday evenings are free from April to December.

hours.note: Thursdays run to 8pm from April through December. Closed Monday and Tuesday, and closed New Year's Day, Independence Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas.

admission.note: Adults $18, seniors 65+ $16, students with ID $7, ages 7 to 18 $6. Free for members and under-7s. Free for everyone Thursday evenings 4pm to 8pm, April through December.

parking: Free on-site parking behind the building.
inside: The Pre-Raphaelite collection
Howard Pyle and the Brandywine illustrators
American art and rotating exhibitions
A cafe and a gift shop
warnings: Closed Monday and Tuesday.
The free Thursday evening only runs April to December. In winter you pay.

sources.label: Delaware Art Museum: visit
sources.note: The operator. Gives Wednesday to Sunday 10am to 4pm, the extended April-to-December Thursdays to 8pm, the full admission table, the free Thursday evening, the Kentmere Parkway address, free on-site parking, the cafe and shop, and the four annual holiday closures.

outstanding: Ask about step-free access and accessible restrooms.
Confirm whether the sculpture garden is open outside museum hours.
Confirm whether the free Thursday needs a booking.

photos.alt: A large stone-edged labyrinth laid out in gravel inside a curved stone wall, bare winter trees behind it, one person walking the far edge.
photos.caption: The labyrinth behind the museum, in winter. Outside, free, and open when the galleries aren't.

name: Hagley Museum and Library
blurb: The original du Pont black powder works on the Brandywine, plus the family's first house and gardens, spread over a couple of hundred acres. Most people spend two to three hours. It's outdoors as much as in, on gravel and uneven ground.

hours.note: Last admission 4pm, and they push you to arrive before 3pm. Wednesdays are pre-booked groups and members only.

admission.note: Adults $22. Students, seniors 62+, veterans and military retirees $18. Ages 6 to 14 $12. Free for under-6s, active military and their families, and members.

website.label: Hagley Museum and Library: hours and tickets

accessibility: A wheelchair-accessible shuttle runs between the main areas. The grounds themselves are uneven with gravel paths, and Hagley says to wear proper shoes.
parking: Free parking by the Visitor Center. You can't drive into the rest of the site.
inside: Nation of Inventors, about 30 to 40 minutes
The Powder Yard along the Brandywine, 40 to 60 minutes
Eleutherian Mills, the du Pont residence, about 45 minutes to an hour
The gardens
A museum store and a cafe by the Visitor Center
warnings: The powder yard is closed 24 August to 4 September 2026. Everything else stays open and general admission is half price for those two weeks.
Closed Wednesdays to general visitors.
Last admission is 4pm for a site that takes two to three hours.

sources.label: Hagley Museum and Library: hours and tickets
sources.note: The operator. Gives six days a week 10am to 5pm with Wednesday closed, the 4pm last admission, the full admission table, and the 24 August to 4 September 2026 powder yard closure with half-price admission.

sources.label: Hagley Museum and Library: visit
sources.note: Gives the Hagley Creek Road address, the phone number, free Visitor Center parking, the wheelchair-accessible shuttle, the warning about uneven gravel terrain, the store and cafe, and the two-to-three-hour visit estimate.

outstanding: Confirm the powder yard reopens 5 September 2026.

photos.alt: A large stone house with black shutters and wisteria over the front, a tour group of about a dozen people standing on the lawn and brick path in front of it.
photos.caption: Eleutherian Mills, the du Pont family house on the Hagley site, with a tour group on the lawn. Public domain, from a U.S. Department of Transportation photograph.

name: Winterthur Museum, Garden & Library
blurb: Henry Francis du Pont's house and his American decorative arts collection, wrapped in a 60-acre garden inside a thousand acres of meadow and woods. Enchanted Woods is the children's garden and is the reason a lot of families come at all.

hours.note: The research library keeps its own hours: Monday to Friday 9am to 4pm for drop-ins, special collections by appointment. Yuletide adds some Friday and Saturday evenings.

admission.note: Adults $29, seniors 62+ and students 13+ $27, groups of 15+ $26, children 3–12 $12, under 3 free. Yuletide runs dearer: $33 adult, $31 senior/student, $12 child. SNAP and EBT cardholders pay $2; active-duty military are free through Blue Star Museums. A general-admission ticket is valid for two consecutive days. Published by Winterthur on its admission and packages page, read 8 August 2026.

inside: The house and the American decorative arts collection
A 60-acre garden with 25 miles of paths
Enchanted Woods, the children's garden
A thousand acres of meadow and woodland
A gift shop and somewhere to eat
warnings: Closed Mondays.
No admission prices are published on the visit page. You find out at checkout.

photos.caption: The house from the drive. It runs to 175 rooms, which is worth knowing before you decide how long you have.

name: New Castle Court House Museum
operator: Delaware Division of Historical and Cultural Affairs
blurb: Delaware's first courthouse and first capitol, built in 1732, in the middle of old New Castle. Free, and guided only — you can't wander it on your own. Tours run every hour or so and take about 45 minutes.

hours.note: Guided tours only. Wednesday to Saturday at 10, 11, 1, 2 and 3; Sunday at 1:30, 2:30 and 3:30. Groups over 10 need to book. Open on Labor Day.

website.label: Delaware Division of Historical and Cultural Affairs: New Castle Court House Museum

accessibility: The first floor is accessible to people with mobility concerns. Nothing published about the upper floors.
parking: Street parking in downtown New Castle.
inside: The 1732 courthouse, a National Historic Landmark
Your Vote, Your Choice
The Path to Freedom, on the Underground Railroad
Three Forts, One Community, on the Swedish, Dutch and English settlements
National Parks Passport stamps
warnings: Guided tours only, on a fixed timetable. Turn up between tours and you wait.
Closed Monday and Tuesday.

sources.label: Delaware Division of Historical and Cultural Affairs: New Castle Court House Museum
sources.note: The operator, a state division. Gives the day-by-day hours including the different Sunday times, the full tour timetable, free admission, the Delaware Street address, the phone number, restrooms, first-floor accessibility, street parking and the exhibit list.

outstanding: Confirm whether the last tour of the day ever fills up.
Ask whether there's a gift shop.
Confirm winter and holiday closures.

photos.alt: A brick colonial courthouse with a white cupola and balcony, three flags flying from it, cars parked along the street in front.
photos.caption: The courthouse from Delaware Street. The cupola is the surveying point the Twelve-Mile Circle was struck from.

name: New Castle County Libraries

hours.note: Every branch keeps its own timetable and the county publishes them per branch. Rather than print a partial week here and have you plan around it, the table below gives you the branch, the address and the number to ring.

name: The Old State House
operator: Delaware Division of Historical and Cultural Affairs
blurb: Delaware's statehouse from 1791, on The Green in Dover. An 18th-century courtroom downstairs and the old legislative chambers upstairs. Free, guided, and about 45 minutes. There are no restrooms in the building.

hours.note: Guided tours at 10, 11, 1, 2 and 3, running no more than 45 minutes. Large groups book ahead on 302-739-9194.

website.label: Delaware Division of Historical and Cultural Affairs: The Old State House

accessibility: The first floor is accessible to people with disabilities. The second floor is up stairs.
parking: Free street parking around The Green, but limited.

The former state legislative chambers upstairs
Portraits of Delaware figures from the War of 1812, and a George Washington
warnings: No restrooms in the building. Plan for that before a tour with children.
Closed Sunday, Monday and Tuesday.

name: Zwaanendael Museum
operator: Delaware Division of Historical and Cultural Affairs
blurb: The Dutch-gabled building on Kings Highway in Lewes, built for the 300th anniversary of the 1631 Swanendael colony. Free, self-guided, and small enough to do properly in half an hour. There are no restrooms inside — they're in the park next door.

hours.note: Closed Sunday and Monday. Self-guided, with staff around to answer questions.

name: Brandywine Zoo
operator: Delaware Division of Parks and Recreation, with the Delaware Zoological Society
blurb: A small AZA-accredited zoo inside Brandywine Park, under five acres, run by Delaware State Parks. Wheelchair and stroller accessible throughout, free parking across the road, and free to walk into from December through February.

hours.note: Last admission 3:30pm. Closed Christmas Day, and can close for weather or construction.

admission.note: December to February it's free. April, November and March: $7 adults, $6 seniors 62+, $5 children 3 to 17. May through October: $9, $8, $7. Under-3s and members always free.

accessibility: The zoo says every exhibit is wheelchair and stroller accessible, though the ground slopes in places. KultureCity sensory-inclusive certified.
parking: Free general parking in Brandywine Park across from the zoo. Accessible spaces by the Education Building.
inside: Under five acres, from common species to highly endangered ones
A contact yard with goats

warnings: This one is outdoors. It's in this section because it has a gate, a ticket and closing time, not because it keeps the rain off.

photos.alt: A small child in a gray long-sleeved top reaching out to touch a black and white goat standing on straw in a walled contact yard, with a wooden ramp and platform behind.

photos.alt: A dense mass of honeybees covering honeycomb behind glass, hundreds of individuals with a few cells of capped comb visible at the edges.

name: Ashland Nature Center
blurb: Four miles of trails through forest, meadow and along the Red Clay Creek, free and open sunrise to sunset, with a creek shallow enough for children to stand in and a dog welcome on a leash. This is an outdoor trip: the building is small.

hours.season: The visitor center hours above are the April-to-October ones. What it does in winter is not published.
hours.note: The trails keep their own hours and are open every day regardless of the building.

admission.note: Free. The Delaware Nature Society says so plainly on its own page for the site.

website.label: Delaware Nature Society: Ashland Nature Center

accessibility: The society lists accessible areas without saying which. Worth ringing 302-239-2334 if it decides the trip.
parking: Its own lot at the nature center. Confirmed first-hand; how quickly it fills at a weekend isn't.
inside: A small ranger station with a gift shop — interesting, and about ten minutes' worth.
About four miles of self-guided trails through forest, meadow and floodplain.
The Red Clay Creek, shallow and gravel-bottomed where the trail meets it — the part children actually end up in.
An outdoor play kitchen.
A pond, and the dipping nets that go with it.
Restrooms and a picnic area.
warnings: NOT a wet-weather answer. The ranger station is worth a look and will hold a child for about ten minutes; everything else here is outside.
The building and the trails keep different hours. The trails are open sunrise to sunset every day; the visitor center is not.
The Ashland Covered Bridge is just outside the entrance and you drive through it. It is one lane and low.

photos.alt: A shallow, clear creek running over pale gravel between wooded banks under a blue sky, with a gravel bar in the foreground and stepping stones upstream.
photos.caption: The Red Clay Creek where the trail meets it. Ankle-deep over gravel here, and clear enough to see the bottom right across.

photos.alt: A large green and brown frog sitting in a green mesh dip net held over a hand.
photos.caption: What comes out of the pond. Caught, looked at, and put straight back.

fieldNotes.author: Site maintainer
fieldNotes.body: Restrooms, walking trails, a ranger station that doubles as the gift shop, and its own parking. The creek is the part worth driving for with small children — shallow, gravel-bottomed and slow where the trail meets it, so they can get in without it being a decision. There's an outdoor play kitchen too.

fieldNotes.author: Site maintainer
fieldNotes.body: Filed under indoors when I added it, which was wrong. Ashland is an outdoor trip — the ranger station is somewhat interesting but would only occupy kids for about ten minutes. It has moved to attractions and no longer answers "somewhere dry when it rains".
